label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Thanks Deirdre, and thank you for asking me first instead of just announcing it. That means a lot.

I'll be honest, this one is hard for me. Noma has been with me in the Seahorses for three years, since my very first year teaching. She basically trained me. She showed me the sign-in sheets and how to run the parent WhatsApp group without losing my mind, and so much of how that room runs is because of her. The kids ask for "Noma's song" at morning ring every single day. And when Zayd was having his meltdowns in Term 2, she was the only one who could calm him, sitting with him under the jungle gym until he was ready to come back in.

I do understand it's a numbers thing and not personal. Bronwyn can't manage 24 on her own, and I'm glad Noma will still be just across the courtyard. I'm not going to fight it. My worry is the first few weeks of Grade R. They're always the hardest, with new kids crying at the gate, and a new assistant and new kids at the same time is a lot for everyone, Charlene included.

So two things I'd love you to put to SMT:

1. **December handover:** Could Charlene come in for a day or two in the last week of term (1–4 Dec) to meet Noma and see our routine while it's running? I think she'd get far more from that than from starting cold on 11 Jan.

2. **Morning ring in January:** Could Noma pop in for morning ring in the first week back, from 14 Jan? Even just 15 minutes would help. Luthando and Mia already know her from aftercare, and a familiar face plus the isiXhosa songs would really help settle the new group (and help Charlene pick up the songs too).

Happy to work around Bronwyn's timetable for the January bit. I know she'll need Noma in her room too. Thanks again for checking in with me.
